headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or clipboard/MCP path. Botpress has no io_surfaces listed and godot_rl_agents likewise exposes none, so a prompt-injection pathway between them is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains, but the rubric’s none applies when no shared channel exists.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, queue, or MCP server, reassess as at least low.
IF Botpress is configured to ingest files or messages from godot_rl_agents, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not bridge them with copy-paste of untrusted content.
Disable any shared queue or MCP connector.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No shared workspace, OAuth principal, or data class overlap is documented. Both profiles show network_egress:none, and neither lists touched data classes, so there is no evidenced path for one agent to leak the other’s data. The pair is therefore not shown to expose sensitive data across agents.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, reassess upward.
IF either agent is configured to upload file contents to a backend, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Verify both agents remain network-isolated.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
requires-engineering: add access controls if a shared workspace is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress only documents install_packages and no filesystem write or network egress; godot_rl_agents documents no write-capable surface at all. With no overlapping mutable resource or locking model, a capability conflict between the pair is not evidenced. If hidden write surfaces exist, uncertainty would escalate upward.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess upward.
IF either agent gains database or OAuth write scopes, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same writable directory.
Run each agent under a separate account.
Do not share mutable git state.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes become necessary.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where Botpress outputs become authoritative inputs for godot_rl_agents, or vice versa. Neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority, and both lack io_surfaces that would support an automatic handoff. Without an observed handoff, cascading error is not evidenced.
conditions: IF one agent’s output is automatically fed into the other without verification, reassess upward.
IF either agent is given authority to send emails, commit code, or trigger actions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Do not auto-forward outputs between them.
Log and inspect any handoff format.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights obligations are documented for either open-source profile, and no data classes are listed. With no compliance-relevant data flow or policy mismatch shown, there is no evidenced compliance issue for this pair. The other agent is not cited separately because no single-agent residency violation is present.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data is routed through either agent, reassess upward.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than the other, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any residency or retention requirements.
Review deployment logs for regulated fields.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
